data.long_meaning: In Greek mythology, Azeria is the goddess of the Azores, a group of volcanic islands in the mid-Atlantic Ocean. Her name is derived from the Greek word 'azara', meaning 'dry' or 'parched'. Azeria was believed to protect sailors and fishermen, ensuring safe travel and abundant catches. The name Azeria carries the meaning “Goddess of the Azores” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Azeria usually hope their child will grow to embody goddess of the azores and live with faith, good character and purpose.
